label: Yevgeny Zamyatin — We
description: Dystopian novel of mathematically regimented collective life, surveillance, desire, revolution, and individuality.

label: H. G. Wells — Men Like Gods
description: Utopian scientific romance depicting a rational advanced society; a direct negative stimulus for Huxley.

label: Fitzgerald — The Great Gatsby
description: Novel of desire, class performance, wealth, reinvention, memory, and the American Dream.

label: Hemingway — The Sun Also Rises
description: Modernist novel of expatriates, war aftermath, masculinity, restraint, and damaged social rituals.

label: Ernest Hemingway
description: Writer whose compressed prose, omission, dialogue, and experience-centered style became a major twentieth-century influence.

label: Faulkner — The Sound and the Fury
description: Modernist family tragedy using fractured chronology and multiple consciousnesses.

label: Aldous Huxley — Brave New World
description: Dystopian satire of engineered happiness, consumption, conditioning, caste, biotechnology, and managed desire.

label: Aldous Huxley
description: Novelist and essayist concerned with technology, conditioning, perception, social organization, and human possibility.

label: Robert E. Howard — Conan stories
description: Sword-and-sorcery stories fusing weird fiction, adventure, invented deep history, and anti-civilizational energy.

label: H. P. Lovecraft / Cthulhu Mythos
description: Cosmic-horror network emphasizing human insignificance, forbidden knowledge, antiquity, and shared invented lore.

label: Great Depression
description: Economic collapse, migration, unemployment, labor conflict, dispossession, and political realignment.

label: Spanish Civil War
description: Civil conflict and ideological struggle experienced directly by Orwell and many international writers.

label: Steinbeck — The Grapes of Wrath
description: Migration novel of dispossession, family, labor, ecology, exploitation, and collective dignity.

label: John Steinbeck
description: Writer associated with California, labor, ecology, working-class communities, biblical patterning, and social realism.

label: Borges — Ficciones
description: Metafictional stories of labyrinths, books, infinity, doubles, invented scholarship, and unstable reality.

label: World War II
description: Total war, genocide, fascism, mass propaganda, nuclear weapons, displacement, and postwar order.

label: George Orwell — Nineteen Eighty-Four
description: Dystopian novel of totalitarian power, surveillance, propaganda, language, memory, and coercive reality.

label: George Orwell
description: Essayist and novelist shaped by imperial service, poverty observation, socialism, the Spanish Civil War, and wartime propaganda.

label: Joseph Campbell — The Hero with a Thousand Faces
description: Popular synthesis of heroic quest patterns that became highly influential in screenwriting and genre discussion.

label: Asimov — I, Robot / robot stories
description: Robot stories formalizing rule-bound machine ethics and human-machine dilemmas.

label: C. S. Lewis — The Chronicles of Narnia
description: Portal fantasy combining Christian allegory, medieval cosmology, fairy tale, myth, and children’s adventure.

label: Bradbury — Fahrenheit 451
description: Dystopian novel of censorship, mass media, distraction, conformity, and preservation of books.

label: Tolkien — The Lord of the Rings
description: Secondary-world epic synthesizing philology, northern myth, medieval literature, Catholic imagination, war experience, and invented languages.

label: J. R. R. Tolkien
description: Philologist, medievalist and fantasy author whose language invention and mythopoesis reshaped modern fantasy.

label: Shirley Jackson — The Haunting of Hill House
description: Psychological Gothic in which architecture, perception, loneliness, and supernatural ambiguity remain entangled.
